brief: A three-storey tower: drawers on the bottom storey and open bins on the top storey.

requirements.evidence: Column at (0,0) runs levels 0-2 (piece 0,0,0 full; 0,0,1 full; 0,0,2 full). A side column at (1,0) has half-w at levels 0 and 1 and a full at level 2, but the level-2 full at 1,0,2 is UNSUPPORTED.
Two slide drawers on level 0: drawer:0#1,0#cut (key e, on half-w 1,0,0) and drawer:0#0,-1#cut (key s, on half-n 0,-1,0).

requirements.requirement: Open bins on the top storey
requirements.evidence: hex-bin-full bins at 0,0,2 and 1,0,2. The bin at 1,0,2 sits on the unsupported base, so it is not structurally held (error UNSUPPORTED).

finish.summary: I built a partial three-storey tower, but check_build still reports one error (UNSUPPORTED on the full base at 1,0,2), so the build is not valid as it stands. I ran out of turns before fixing it. I did not run capOpenFaces or lockJoints, and I did not dress the build. The LOOSE_BODY warnings on the side cells would clear with joint bolts from lockJoints, but that does not fix the unsupported error.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
